summary: Frenchman's Island Light in Oneida Lake, New York: a concrete canal-era tower started in 1917 and lit in 1918, given a steel top in 1949, and reached only by boat.

structures.type: round concrete tower with gallery on a square base

access.note: Reached only by boat, with a rustic dock. The site is open and the tower is closed (Rowlett). The archive lists it as not open to the public.

facts.agency: New York State Canals (owner/operator); New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (site manager)

events.note: State contract 132 awarded to Lupfer & Remick of Buffalo; work begun on three concrete towers for Lake Oneida (Frenchman's Island tower came later)
Work on the Frenchman's Island tower started in summer 1917, after preparatory work
Light activated the year after the Verona Beach and Brewerton lights (lit late summer 1917); gas beacon
20-foot steel skeletal tower mounted atop the concrete tower; focal plane raised 20 feet
New York State Parks reopened the island after years of closure for vandalism
Island transferred to the Department of Environmental Conservation as a wildlife preserve (directory wording: "transferred to 2011")

corrections.current: Taken from sources that give no usable position for this light
corrections.proposed: Position confirmed by Lighthouse Friends: 43.219626, -76.051215, within a few metres of the record point 43.219612, -76.051204
corrections.why: Lighthouse Friends gives Frenchman's Island Light on Frenchman's Island in Oneida Lake at 43.219626, -76.051215. The record's coordinates agree with it, so the status note is out of date.
The record leaves water blank. Lighthouse Friends and the archive both place the light in Oneida Lake (the archive says Lake Oneida).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The archive gives Open to Public: No. Rowlett's directory describes the 2008 reopening of the island to the public and says it is accessible only by boat. The story reports both and does not settle the question.

Lighthouse Friends gives an 85-foot concrete tower; Rowlett gives 85 feet plus a 20-foot steel skeletal tower (105 feet), with a focal plane of 123 feet. The numbers are consistent with an 18-foot knoll.

notes_for_editor: Thin station: three independent sources (Lighthouse Friends, Rowlett's directory and the USLHS archive) plus one local history (Orzell, Verona Beach Lighthouse Association). No keeper is named in any source read here. The USLHS archive has no roster for this light (roster.py: none listed), so keepers is empty. The 1920 state keepers' program is general context from Lighthouse Friends, not a record of this light. No primary record was found: New York State Canal Department reports for 1916 to 1918 are not in the corpus, and a Chronicling America search of New York papers for 1916 to 1919 returned nothing. Lighthouse Friends writes 'Fisherman's Island' twice where it means Frenchman's Island; the story uses Frenchman's Island. Rowlett's directory says the island was 'transferred to 2011'; the story gives 2011 as the transfer year and the quote in evidence keeps the directory's wording. The record's status note says the position is unusable; the coordinates agree with Lighthouse Friends (see corrections). The record's name, county and water fields: water is Oneida Lake per the sources. County was not checked and is left blank. The record's photos (Wikimedia Commons, 1917 image) were not checked for licence and were not used. Fact-check 2026-10-28: Orzell gives the contract's towers as built 'since 1915' and spells the firm 'Lufer & Remick'; Lighthouse Friends gives work from 1916 and spells it 'Lupfer & Remick'. The story follows Lighthouse Friends and gives no build year for the contract. Lighthouse Friends says 'about twenty miles' (not nautical miles), and the story now says miles. Rowlett's sentence gives the transfer only as 'transferred to 2011' (garbled); the story says so and the 2011 event rests on that wording alone.
